subject: Urgent: Unexpected 429s impacting CloudWave data pipelines — remediation steps & postmortem follow-up

Subject: Re: Strange spike of 429s in prod starting 09:05 PST

Hi team,

Starting ~09:05 PST our ingestion pipelines began returning a high volume of 429s for calls to the Redwood generation endpoint (model: rw-large). We've seen retries back off but the queues are filling; this has caused a ~15 minute lag across five datastreams.

Attached are a zipped snippet of request logs (cloudwave-request-logs-20251114.zip) and a small sample of the failing payloads. Our SREs confirmed no client-side throttling changed on our end. Can you confirm whether any quota or rate-limit changes were deployed on your side in the last hour?

Impact: several downstream jobs delayed, some missed SLA windows.

Request: immediate mitigation and a short postmortem; our product team needs the root cause and timeline.

Thanks,
Ben Kelley
Senior SRE, CloudWave Analytics

On Fri, Nov 14, 2025 at 09:20 AM sean.gallagher@redwood.ai wrote:
> Ben / CloudWave team — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the disruption.
>
> Immediate plan: 1) I am escalating to our infra team (cc'd: Dev) to triage quota/config state; 2) Monica from Customer Success will coordinate status updates and any temporary credits; 3) I'll share remediation steps once Dev confirms the cause.

Quick technical update from infra: we identified the root cause — an automated quota-sync job rolled out a stricter per-customer rate window for a subset of customers due to a bad mapping rule. CloudWave's account id matched a staging pattern in the mapping, which applied a 60r/min limit instead of the expected 600r/min for their tier. The change deployed at 08:58 PST, which aligns with your observed failures.

Actions taken (completed by 09:35 PST):
- Rolled back the mapping change to the previous mapping set
- Applied an emergency override to restore CloudWave's quota to 600r/min
- Warmed KV caches and cleared per-connection rate trackers for the affected frontends

We are continuing to run a targeted validation sweep across similar mapping rules and will push a fix to the quota-sync job to validate customer id patterns before applying changes.

Attachment: redwood-remediation-runbook.pdf (application/pdf) — contains rollback steps and immediate mitigation checklist.

Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Postmortem: 2025-11-14 quota-sync mapping error — summary & remediation

Hi Emma / Ben — thank you again for your patience. Attached is a concise postmortem summary (postmortem-summary-20251118.pdf) and the corrective action plan. High-level timeline and findings below.

Timeline (PST):
- 08:58 — quota-sync job deployed mapping change (automated rollout)
- 09:05 — CloudWave starts seeing 429s from production calls
- 09:12 — CloudWave notified Redwood via ops@cloudwave.com
- 09:20 — Sean escalated to infra and CS; Dev engaged
- 09:35 — Remediation rollback and quota override applied; traffic normalized

Root cause: a staging-pattern mis-evaluation in the quota-sync mapping logic incorrectly matched CloudWave's account id, applying a much lower per-minute rate limit. The root cause was a missing boundary check in the pattern-matching function, combined with insufficient canary coverage for mapping rollouts.

Corrective actions (short/medium term):
- Fix mapping logic to include explicit boundary checks (in code) — Target: 2025-11-21
- Add pre-rollout verification tests and a dry-run mode for the quota-sync job — Target: 2025-11-20
- Extend rollout canaries to include at least two production customers and add automatic rollback on anomaly detection — Target: 2025-11-24
- Offer CloudWave a one-time credit for the affected window (Laura will confirm amount) and a follow-up health check call in two weeks.

If you prefer a live review, we are available Wed, Nov 19 or Thu, Nov 20 in the morning PST. Monica will coordinate logistics and the invite.

Appended: brief remediation checklist and links to the JIRA ticket: JIRA-INF-4821 and Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/s/incident-2025-11-14-cloudwave-postmortem

Thanks again — we take this seriously and are prioritizing the rollout-safety work to avoid recurrence.

—Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
